text:
neil-cs: FYI Cedarbrook just opened a ticket — saying p99 spikes on text-gen endpoints since yesterday afternoon. customer reports timeouts and UI slowdowns.

maria-sre: saw the alert chain. p95 is fine but p99 jumped to ~2.8s on their tenant for several models. They sent traces showing long queue wait and a couple of "no capacity" 503s.

aj-platform: can you paste the request IDs / tenant_id? I want to check routing and per-tenant queue stats.

neil-cs: tenant id `cedarbrook-01`. Sample req: `req_20260315_314159`. They included this stack snippet: ```error: upstream 503 -> "no capacity available for tenant" at router.go:412```

maria-sre: grabbing logs now. quick check: traffic for cedarbk spiked ~3x between 15:10-15:45 UTC yesterday, mostly from embedding jobs + a few large chat sessions.

devon-eng: that matches our telemetry — their concurrent sequences hit 42 at one point which trips per-tenant backpressure rules (threshold is 30 for shared pool). Could be noisy neighbor.

aj-platform: opening a short block: adjusting tenant throttle to allowlist for burst? We can add them to short reservation pool if infra approves.

maria-sre: before we do that, can we confirm tail latencies are queuing vs. model decode? SLOs differ depending on where the latency lives.

sre-bot: [incident-digest] p99 spikes detected for tenant cedarbk-01 across route /v1/generate-text at 2026-03-14T15:12:xxZ. CPU eff ~82%, GPU util ~65% on nodes serving that shard.

devon-eng: I pulled KV cache hit rates — low for their workload (few repeat prefixes). Batching patterns show one huge req that serialized 15 items in a single call (long prompt list) which created contention.

neil-cs: customer says they batched some user uploads into a single job overnight. They didn't realize it would hammer shared capacity. They're asking for an allowlist to prevent throttles because these jobs are critical for nightly syncs.

maria-sre: propose 3-step plan: 1) immediate mitigation: temporary reservation (2 hours) to clear backlog, 2) add to a "managed-burst" allowlist with rate limits and quota checks, 3) recommend long-term: dedicated capacity or reroute heavy batch jobs to offline pipelines. Thoughts?

aj-platform: +1. infra constraints: we have two spare GPUs in region-us-west-2 that are currently idle. We can spin a short-lived reservation for cedarbk-01 for 4 hours if sales approves the chargeback. I'll start the reservation job:```shell
# allocate 2 GPUs for tenant
rdmctl reserve --tenant cedarbk-01 --gpus 2 --duration 4h --note "temp mitigation for p99 spike"
```

devon-eng: while reservation spins up, we should apply a per-tenant soft-throttle rule to prevent another huge batch from queuing and killing the pool. Something like: max_concurrency=20, max_batch_size=8.

maria-sre: agree. Applying a soft throttle now so we don't have another queue meltdown.

maria-sre: ```json
{"tenant":"cedarbk-01","max_concurrency":20,"max_batch_size":8,"action":"soft_throttle"}
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Throttle policy applied to tenant cedarbk-01.

neil-cs: told the customer we will reserve capacity and put a throttle in place; they asked if we can whitelist their IPs to avoid automated per-request rate-limiting that hits their syncs. They provided a list: `34.120.12.8/32`, `34.120.12.9/32`.

aj-platform: IP allowlist is different from capacity allowlist. We can add IPs to their tenant-level access control, but that won't bypass resource-based backpressure. Must communicate that clearly.

devon-eng: also found one node with a spiky network egress causing slow model pulls which made decoding slower for a subset of requests. I'll mark it as degraded and re-route its shards.

sre-bot: [scaling-action] migrated shard gw-72 -> gw-79 to reduce tail. Expected effect: p99 drop by ~20-30% for affected requests.

maria-sre: reservation is up (aj confirmed). Customer traffic moved to reserved pool. Early telemetry: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.1s for the next 30 minutes.

neil-cs: customer verifies UI responsiveness has improved. They asked for a follow-up to get permanent guardrails.

aj-platform: next steps: 1) draft a runbook for cedarbk-01 recommending dedicated small reservation (2 GPUs) for nightly batch window 02:00-06:00 UTC or schedule batch windows to off-peak, 2) update tenant policy to allow IP-based bypass only for auth/ingress rate limits (not compute backpressure), 3) offer a temporary credit for the emergency reservation.

devon-eng: will open PR to add a new tenancy profile `managed-burst` with explicit rate-limits + telemetry hooks so CS can see queued requests per job.

maria-sre: please include an alert rule for "sustained queued > 20 for tenant X" that pings cs + eng-sre. We missed the early signs.

sre-bot: [alert-created] rule tenant_queued_threshold created for cedarbk-01.

neil-cs: I'll draft the customer-facing note: explain root cause = large batched jobs causing queue/backpressure, mitigation = reservation + throttle, next steps = recommend dedicated night reservation or pipeline changes. Will send in 30m.

maria-sre: good. Also capture the repro steps for eng-runbook: 1) reproduce by issuing 15 concurrent long-sequence requests from same tenant, 2) monitor queued_requests metric, 3) see backpressure 503s -> apply soft throttle / spin reservation.

devon-eng: repro snippet for local test:```python
import requests
for i in range(15):
  requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json={"tenant":"cedarbk-01","prompt":"x"*2000})
```

maria-sre: closing loop — customer confirmed recovery, cs will follow up on product options. Marking this thread resolved but keeping links to logs.

neil-cs: resolved from support side. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
